# ActBeCalf external transfer challenge

This pipeline evaluates whether an activity model trained on the Kaggle Cow Nose Ring cohort transfers to a separately collected cattle cohort. It is an **activity-perception** benchmark; it does not train an autonomous policy or estimate natural time budgets.

## Source and scope

The external file is the official Zenodo v1.0 `AcTBeCalf.csv` (DOI `10.5281/zenodo.13259482`), whose Zenodo API metadata declares CC BY 4.0. The Kaggle mirror found during the audit has an unknown license and is not used. The official file is 177,608,717 bytes with 2,467,162 rows, 30 pre-weaned Holstein Friesian/Jersey calves, 25 Hz neck-collar accelerometry, and 21 base behaviors represented by 50 observed composite labels. The study reports 27.4 labeled hours, 0.91 hours per calf on average, collected from one Irish research farm. Video periods were selected to include active behavior, so these labels do not describe daily prevalence. In the pinned 5 s extraction, only 127 rumination windows occur across 6 calves, so rumination recall and macro-F1 have high uncertainty.

The model training side remains the pinned Kaggle Cow Nose Ring CSV (CC0-1.0, SHA-256 in `training/train.py`). Training uses Kaggle's GPU runtime for the frozen Torch MLP; ExtraTrees is CPU-based by design. The external test file is attached to a private Kaggle dataset created from the official Zenodo file and carries the DOI, license, and attribution in its metadata. No raw measurements or per-animal output are committed.

## Frozen experiment

The CNR 5-code parser maps `feeding -> feeding`, `rumination -> rumination`, and `standing/lying/walking -> other`. ActBeCalf maps `eating` and its observed modifiers (`eating_forage`, `eating_concentrates`, `eating_bedding`) to `feeding`; `rumination` and `rumination_lying` to `rumination`; every other observed composite label (including milk/water drinking) to `other`. The loader validates the 50 observed raw label values and rejects unknown labels rather than silently treating them as `other`. Each side uses the same 18 summary features over disjoint five-second windows. ActBeCalf windows never cross a calf, `segId`, or timestamp gap. No external data is used to fit, normalize, tune, or choose thresholds.

The two frozen candidates are ExtraTrees (the validation-selected v5 family/configuration) and the v5 CUDA MLP architecture/settings. The report also includes a constant baseline set to the majority class in the CNR training split, prediction counts, window-pooled and per-calf macro-F1, per-class metrics, and a 2,000-replicate bootstrap interval that resamples calves as groups. The per-calf score averages F1 only across classes with labeled windows for that calf; predictions to another class still reduce recall for the true class. This external result is exploratory and post-selection because the source CNR cohort, model families, and earlier holdouts were already inspected.

A successful run still tests only one external farm/cohort and simultaneously shifts age, breed, management, sensor placement, and sampling frequency. It cannot isolate which shift caused errors and cannot establish generalization across farms. The 3-class transfer ontology also hides distinctions such as posture, walking, play, drinking, and social behavior.

## Reproduction

1. Fetch `AcTBeCalf.csv` from `https://zenodo.org/api/records/13259482/files/AcTBeCalf.csv/content`; record and verify SHA-256 before training.
2. Create a **private** Kaggle dataset with the official CSV and accompanying attribution/CC BY 4.0 metadata. Do not use or redistribute the Kaggle mirror with unknown rights.
3. Attach that dataset and `fandaoerji/cow-nose-ring-data-set` to the Kaggle script generated by `build_actbecalf_bundle.py`; enable GPU and run the bundled entrypoint.
4. Preserve the Kaggle output artifacts privately. Commit only aggregate metrics, source hashes, split/protocol details, and output artifact hashes after inspecting the completed run.

## Frozen v1 result (Kaggle version 3)

The T4/CUDA run completed with 17,699 external windows from 30 calves. The CNR-training-majority baseline, frozen ExtraTrees, and frozen CUDA MLP all predicted `other` for every window. Each therefore had pooled macro-F1 0.3039 and weighted-F1 0.7638; feeding and rumination F1 were both zero. The macro-F1 exactly matches the constant baseline, so this is a negative external-transfer result and neither checkpoint is suitable for runtime integration. The 127 rumination windows across six calves also make that class estimate unstable. See the aggregate reproducibility record at `training/experiments/cnr-to-actbecalf-external-transfer-v1-manifest.json`.

Version 1 did not train: the initial bundle accidentally invoked the loader's CLI entrypoint at import time. The bundle builder now strips that entrypoint, and version 3 completed with the corrected runner and explicit baseline. The model artifacts remain private and are represented in the record only by hashes.

Local parser tests:

```sh
python -m pytest training/external/test_actbecalf.py
```
